tools.name: analyze_audio
tools.description: Analyze original source audio from cached waveform peaks; local, read-only, no model. Returns bounded peak/RMS waveform bins, onset candidates and signed energy changes (dB), all in source µs (`src_*`), plus resolution and event counts. Choose music edit/alignment points, including outside a clip's trim. These are amplitude measurements, not beats, bars or melody recognition. At most 60 s per call; max_points affects only the summary. Peaks are cache-limited, not true-peak or LUFS. To land `src_us` at timeline T on a layer: `src_in_us = src_us - (T - t_start_us) * rate` (`rate` from project://tracks, 1 when absent).

max_points.description: Maximum waveform summary bins, 1..1000 (default 200). Does not change event detection resolution.

media_id.description: Imported Audio or Video media id; analyzes its original audio before mix/effects.

onset_threshold_db.description: Minimum short-time energy rise for onset candidates, 1..30 dB (default 6). Candidates are not beats or melody labels.

src_end_us.description: Source-absolute end, exclusive. Default start + 60 seconds, capped at media end. At most 60 seconds per call.

src_start_us.description: Source-absolute start in microseconds, inclusive. Default 0.

tools.name: ping
tools.description: Liveness check. Returns 'pong' to confirm the WeftCut MCP server is reachable.

tools.name: detect_pauses
tools.description: Find the pauses in a clip's audio — the stretches nobody is speaking — from the pre-computed waveform. Read-only: the write is `remove_pauses` (cut them) or `create_tacks` (point the user at them). A pause is a run where every channel's peak stays below `threshold_amp` for at least `min_pause_us`; a loud run shorter than `bridge_us` inside it (a click, a cough) does not end it. Defaults `threshold_amp=0.02` (-34 dBFS), `min_pause_us=500000`, `bridge_us=80000` (must be below `min_pause_us`). `layer_id` is an Audio layer, or a VideoClip, which resolves to the Audio layer of its link (refused when it plays no sound). Returns `{ pauses: [{ t_start_us, t_end_us }], noise_floor_amp, peaks_source }`, timeline-absolute µs, sorted; `noise_floor_amp` is the 10th-percentile peak (a threshold reads well at the floor + 6 dB); `peaks_source` is "raw" or "fx" (baked effect chain). Refused (`DerivativeNotReady`) until the waveform job finishes; retry in a few seconds.

bridge_us.description:
A loud run shorter than this (µs) inside a quiet run does not end the
pause. Default 80000 (80ms). Must be ≥ 0 and below `min_pause_us`.

layer_id.description:
Target Audio layer id. A VideoClip id is accepted by the host, which
resolves it to the Audio layer of its link before the call.

min_pause_us.description: Shortest pause to surface, in microseconds. Default 500000 (0.5s).

threshold_amp.description:
Peak amplitude threshold in [0.0, 1.0]. Anything strictly below this
counts as quiet. Default 0.02 (≈ -34 dBFS).

tools.name: analyze_clip
tools.description: Detect shot boundaries in a VideoClip layer. Deterministic, over the source (720p proxy preferred). Returns `{ media_id, mapping, shots: [{ index, src_start_us, src_end_us, src_keyframe_us, brightness, motion, sharpness, flags }], cut_scores: [{ src_us, score }] }` in source µs, clipped to the source the layer plays; `mapping` places them on the timeline: t = t_start_us + (src - src_in_us) / rate. `shots` is the cleaned segmentation (cuts closer than `min_shot_us` merged), `cut_scores` the raw cut signal (0..1). Per shot: `src_keyframe_us` is the midpoint cover frame; `brightness` mean luma 0..1; `sharpness` variance of the Laplacian (higher = sharper); `motion` 0..1 endpoint difference; `flags` may hold "black", "freeze", "fade". Optional `sensitivity` (0..1, default 0.4; lower = more cuts), `min_shot_us` (default 500000), `passes` (subset of "shots" / "stats" / "events", default all — drop "stats" / "events" for timing only). VideoClip layers only. To split at every cut in one edit use `auto_split_by_shot`.

min_shot_us.description:
Minimum shot duration (microseconds); cuts closer than this are merged.
Default 500000 (0.5 seconds).

passes.description:
Which passes to run — a subset of `["shots", "stats", "events"]`.
Default all. Drop `"stats"` / `"events"` to skip per-shot frame sampling
and return timing only.

sensitivity.description:
Cut sensitivity in [0.0, 1.0]: a frame whose shot-change score exceeds
this starts a new shot. Lower = more (finer) cuts. Default 0.4.

tools.name: compare_frames
tools.description: Compare two video frames for perceptual similarity — dedup shots, match a cutaway. Each side is `{ layer_id, src_us }`: a VideoClip layer and a source µs time (the space of `analyze_clip`'s `src_keyframe_us` and `media://{id}/frame/{src_us}`); the two may be the same clip or different clips. Returns `{ phash_hamming, ssim, similar }`: `phash_hamming` is the 0..64 distance between the frames' perceptual hashes (0 = identical, 20+ = a different scene), `ssim` is structural similarity 0..1, and `similar` is `phash_hamming <= 10 && ssim >= 0.5`. Read-only; VideoClip layers only, errors naming the offending side.

src_us.description:
Source-absolute microseconds of the frame to sample (the space
`analyze_clip`'s `src_keyframe_us` uses).

Source-absolute microseconds of the frame to sample (the space
`analyze_clip`'s `src_keyframe_us` uses).

tools.name: import_media
tools.description: Import ONE media file. Hashes it (blake3) and probes it with ffprobe when installed. Returns `{ media_id, kind, label, path, path_rel, duration_us, width, height, has_audio }`: `path` is the pooled copy in the project's Media/ folder (`copying: true` while it is copied from the source); `relinked: true` when a pooled item whose file was gone now reads this one. A subtitle (.srt/.vtt/.ass) is pooled for `apply_subtitles`. A directory, a missing path or an unreadable file is refused by name before anything is written; a read that fails mid-import rolls the provisional pool row back. A pooled file answers `existing: true`; `same_content_as` names copies of its bytes. Unrecorded.

path.description: Path to a video / audio / image / subtitle file the host can read: absolute, or relative to the open project's folder.

tools.name: extract_clip_audio
tools.description: Extract a VideoClip or Audio layer's ORIGINAL source audio — before gain, mute, effects or mixing — for an agent running its own speech model; no engine or API key is involved and nothing is uploaded. Returns a JSON metadata block (`layer_id`, `media_id`, `t_start_us`, `t_end_us`, `src_in_us`, `src_out_us`, `duration_us`, `rate` {num, den}, `sample_rate_hz`, `channels`, `bits_per_sample`, `byte_length`, `mime_type`) plus an MCP audio block: base64 WAV, mono 16 kHz 16-bit, starting at zero. Optional `t_start_us`/`t_end_us` are timeline µs, defaulting to the layer endpoints; at most 60 s of source audio per call — timeline windows ≤ 60 s / rate. Map a WAV offset `w` to the timeline as `t_start_us + w / rate`, then `apply_transcripts`. Refuses a layer with no audio, a window outside the layer (a VideoClip's audio is its own stream, not its linked Audio layer).

layer_id.description: Target VideoClip or Audio layer id.

t_end_us.description:
Exclusive window end in the owning composition's absolute microseconds.
Defaults to the layer end. Maximum window duration: 60000000 us (60 s).

t_start_us.description:
Window start in the owning composition's absolute microseconds.
Defaults to the layer start. Must lie inside the layer.

tools.name: transcribe_clip
tools.description: Transcribe a VideoClip or Audio layer with the configured engine (cloud OpenAI Whisper, local whisper.cpp / FunASR, or an OpenAI-compatible server). Returns `{ backend, segments: [{ t_start_us, t_end_us, text, words: [{ t_start_us, t_end_us, text }] }], language, word_timing }` in timeline-absolute µs. Hand the envelope to `apply_transcripts` to lay captions that keep the word timing. `word_timing` is "exact" or "interpolated_from_cue". Optional `t_start_us`/`t_end_us` narrow the window; `backend` ("openai" | "whisper_cpp" | "funasr" | "byo_endpoint") REQUIRES that engine — it errors naming the missing key / binary / model / URL rather than substituting, so a local choice never uploads; omitted, the user's preferred engine then availability. `word_timestamps` (default true) asks for exact per-word times where the engine can (OpenAI is SRT-only). Retimed segment and word times are projected onto the timeline. Network engines get audio over 10 min in pieces cut at pauses. Errors name the cause: no engine, rate limits, auth, timeouts.

backend.description:
Strict engine override: `"openai"` | `"whisper_cpp"` | `"funasr"` |
`"byo_endpoint"`. That engine serves or the call errors; nothing is
substituted. Omitted: the user's preferred engine, then availability.

language.description: Optional ISO-639-1 language hint (`"en"`, `"zh"`). Auto-detect when omitted.

layer_id.description: Target VideoClip or Audio layer id.

normalize_audio.description:
Explicit opt-in: normalize only the transcription copy toward -3 dBFS
peak, at most +24 dB. Original media/timeline stay unchanged. Default false.

t_end_us.description:
Optional transcription window end in timeline microseconds.
Defaults to the layer's `t_end_us`. Must lie within the layer.

t_start_us.description:
Optional transcription window start in timeline microseconds.
Defaults to the layer's `t_start_us`. Must lie within the layer.

word_timestamps.description:
Ask for exact per-word times where the engine can emit them. Default
true; `false` forces SRT-style interpolated words. The result's
`word_timing` reports what you got.

tools.name: synthesize_speech
tools.description: Synthesize speech with the configured cloud TTS provider (OpenAI tts-1) and place it as an Audio layer. `text` ≤ 4096 chars; `voice` is one of alloy / echo / fable / onyx / nova / shimmer; optional `speed` 0.25..4.0 (default ≈ 1.0); optional `target_track_id` (default: the first Audio track, else a new 'Voiceover' track); optional `t_start_us` (default: the composition's current duration, so the clip appends at the end). The MP3 is cached by `(model, voice, speed, text)`, so a repeat call costs no API request. Returns `{ layer_id, media_id, t_start_us, t_end_us, cached }`.

speed.description: 0.25..4.0 for tts-1. Omit to use the provider default (~1.0).

t_start_us.description:
Optional timeline start in microseconds. Defaults to the composition's
current `duration_us` so the voiceover appends at the end.

target_track_id.description:
Optional Audio track id. If omitted, lands on the first existing Audio
track or auto-creates one labeled "Voiceover".

text.description: Text to synthesize. tts-1 caps at 4096 characters.

voice.description: Voice identifier. tts-1 accepts: alloy, echo, fable, onyx, nova, shimmer.

tools.name: describe_clip
tools.description: Describe a VideoClip layer's visual content as timestamped segments with a video-understanding model (local Qwen3-VL / MiniCPM-V, or an OpenAI-compatible endpoint). Samples the whole window at `fps` (default 1.0), 16 frames per request (endpoints: configurable), ≤3600 frames per call. Returns `{ backend, model, summary?, media_id, mapping, segments: [{ src_start_us, src_end_us, text, tags }] }`: source µs, placed on the timeline by `mapping` as `analyze_clip`'s are; `text` is prose, `tags` short visual keywords; long windows add a `summary`. Cached per source range; an interrupted call resumes; `refresh` re-describes. `src_start_us`/`src_end_us` (e.g. a shot's) narrow the window; `focus` ("general" | "shot-type") steers `tags`; `language` (BCP-47, default: UI language). `backend` ("qwen3_vl" | "minicpm_v" | "byo_endpoint") REQUIRES that engine and errors naming what is missing, never substituting, so a local choice never uploads frames; omitted: preferred engine, then availability (local first).

backend.description:
Strict engine override: `"qwen3_vl"` | `"minicpm_v"` | `"byo_endpoint"`.
That engine serves or the call errors; nothing is substituted. Omitted:
the user's preferred engine, then availability.

focus.description:
`"general"` or `"shot-type"` (biases `tags` toward shot type / camera).
Default: the app's setting, else `"general"`. Cache key.

fps.description:
Frames sampled per second (higher = finer, more requests). Default:
the app's setting, else 1.0. Cache key.

language.description:
BCP-47 tag the `text` and `tags` come back in (`"en-US"`, `"zh-CN"`,
`"ja"`). Default: the app's UI language. Cache key.

purpose.description:
Cache purpose: clip content (default) or individual shot identification.
Independent of prompt focus; results are never shared across purposes.

refresh.description:
Describe again even when cached, replacing the earlier run (default
false).

src_end_us.description:
Optional exclusive window end, source-absolute microseconds. Defaults to
the end of the source the layer plays. Must lie within it.

src_start_us.description:
Optional window start, source-absolute microseconds (the space the
answer's segments and `analyze_clip`'s shots use). Defaults to the start
of the source the layer plays. Must lie within it.

resources.name: Current project
resources.description: The full open WeftCut project as JSON. Re-fetch after change events.

resources.name: Composition
resources.description: Canvas size, fps, sample rate, color space, background.

resources.name: Media pool
resources.description: All imported media items keyed by id.

resources.name: Tracks
resources.description: Tracks with layer envelopes. Read project://layers/{id} for full layer detail.

resources.name: Compositions
resources.description: Every composition — the root and each Group — with id, label, duration_us and ref_count (how many CompositionRef layers place it). project://tracks?composition=<id> and project://markers?composition=<id> read one of them; unscoped they read the root.

resources.name: History
resources.description: Recent operations and named checkpoints (no snapshots). `ops` is a window: `window_start` is the absolute stack index of `ops[0]`, and `cursor` is absolute too — never an offset into `ops`; absolute indices are the only ones `jump_to` accepts. `evicted` > 0 means the oldest entries were dropped for good.

resources.name: Audio mix plan
resources.description: Compiled export-audio mix plan (layer placement on the 48 kHz frame grid + envelope summaries) — for agents that want structural reasoning about what export will mix.

resources.name: Audio meter
resources.description: Latest preview master-bus level reading (rms/peak dBFS). `live: false` when nothing has played in the last 2 seconds.

prompts.name: cut-pauses
prompts.description: Cut the pauses out of a clip and close the gaps, tightening it. Or tack them first, so the user reviews every pause before any of it goes.

arguments.name: layer_id
arguments.description: Target Audio layer id, or the VideoClip that plays it — a VideoClip is resolved to the Audio layer of its link.

arguments.name: threshold_amp
arguments.description: Peak amplitude threshold in [0.0, 1.0]. Default 0.02 (≈ -34 dBFS).

arguments.name: min_pause_us
arguments.description: Shortest pause to cut, in microseconds. Default 500000 (0.5s).

arguments.name: pad_us
arguments.description: Microseconds of each pause kept on EACH side when removing. Default 100000 (100ms); 0 erases each pause whole.

prompts.name: auto-caption
prompts.description: Transcribe a video or audio layer with the configured engine, then lay the transcript on the caption tracks with its word timing.

arguments.name: layer_id
arguments.description: Target VideoClip or Audio layer id.

arguments.name: language
arguments.description: Optional ISO-639-1 language hint (en, zh, etc.). Auto-detect when omitted.

prompts.name: voiceover
prompts.description: Generate cloud TTS for a script and attach it as an Audio layer.

arguments.name: script
arguments.description: Text to speak. tts-1 caps a single call at 4096 chars; for longer scripts split into paragraphs.

arguments.name: voice
arguments.description: OpenAI voice: alloy, echo, fable, onyx, nova, or shimmer. Required — `synthesize_speech` takes no default.

arguments.name: speed
arguments.description: Optional speech speed in [0.25, 4.0]. Omit for the provider default.

arguments.name: target_track_id
arguments.description: Optional Audio track id. Defaults to the first existing Audio track or a new 'Voiceover' track.
